item.title: Singer-songwriter Mélissa Laveaux: 'Women need more positions of power in the music industry'
item.description: One of France's top musical artists has spoken to FRANCE 24 about the need to empower more women in music. Mélissa Laveaux is currently taking part in the "Les Femmes s'en mêlent" or "Women get involved" festival, which is holding a series of events across the country in an initiative that started nearly 30 years ago and is still going today. The aim is to address the underrepresentation of female artists at music festivals. She spoke to us in Perspective.

item.title: Ukraine: Two bridges in Kyiv heavily damaged by Russian strikes
item.description: Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv while Ukraine struck Moscow's link to annexed Crimea for the second night in a row, officials said Tuesday, ahead of a historic meeting of Chinese, US and Russian leaders. Detals from the ground by FRANCE 24 correspondent in Kyiv, Gulliver Cragg.

item.title: Ukraine strikes major Russian bridge in Crimea with drones and missiles
item.description: Ukrainian drones and missiles struck a vital bridge linking Russia to the occupied Crimean Peninsula, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said Tuesday, calling it an “unprecedented” operation as Russia reported that its forces downed a record number of Ukrainian drones for the second straight day. Meanwhile, Russia struck two major bridges in Kyiv.

item.title: Two Marseille drug traffickers sentenced to life in prison over triple murder
item.description: Two figures in Marseille’s drug trafficking ring were sentenced to life in prison on Monday over a triple murder committed in 2020. Among the victims was Brahim Chabane, the older brother of anti-drug activist and deputy mayor of Marseille Amine Kessaci.

item.title: French presidential debate: 'Le Pen exposed xenophobic and authoritarian aspects of her policies'
item.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Damien Lecomte, French political scientist, researcher, and lecturer at the University of Paris 1 Panthéon-Sorbonne. With five months to go before France's presidential election, Marine Le Pen leads the opinion polls, while Jean-Luc Mélenchon emerges as her most likely second-round opponent. Lecomte says that "the other candidates are basically fighting for the second spot" and that the center and right are "desperately trying to find a way to avoid a second round" between the two. He also warns that a Le Pen presidency could "really change the political life with more xenophobic and nationalistic policies,"even if her ability to secure a parliamentary majority remains uncertain.

item.title: COP31: Corporate interests gain access to govt delegations participating in climate negotiations
item.description: Eve Irvine is pleased to welcome Siphesihle Mvundla, South African Climate and Energy Justice Campaigner at groundWork, a non-profit environmental justice organization. At COP31 in Turkey, representatives of major polluting industries have gained access to climate negotiations through government delegations, accredited organisations and other participation arrangements, according to research by the Kick Big Polluters Out coalition. Mvundla questions the extent of their involvement: "This year particularly, it's not just about the numbers, but it's about the influence that these private interests would have on the negotiations." While businesses have a role in implementing climate action, he questions their access to negotiations intended to regulate their industries and is calling for "an end to big polluter sponsorship and partnership at climate conferences" and insisted: "No more allowing big polluters to write the rules of climate action."

item.description: Has your doctor asked whether they can use artificial intelligence to take notes during an exam? It's very popular, and here's how to think through the pros and the cons of the new technology.

item.title: Third US aircraft carrier arrives in the Middle East as Iran targets Bahrain
item.description: A third American aircraft carrier has arrived in the Middle East, US Central Command said in a social media post Monday, making a dramatic show of military might as President Donald Trump keeps his options open for next steps in the Iran war. It comes as Tehran said Sunday that its forces carried out a drone attack on a US radar system at a helicopter base in the Gulf kingdom of Bahrain.

item.title: Saudi Arabia replaces military commander after Yemen setbacks
item.description: Saudi Arabia replaced the commander overseeing its coalition against Yemen's Iran-allied Houthis on Monday after Riyadh's Yemeni allies were forced to withdraw from swathes of territory in a major setback for their campaign against the group.

item.title: 5 European countries aim to send rejected asylum seekers to Rwanda
item.description: A group of European countries announced Monday that they aim to set up a “return hub” in Rwanda where rejected asylum seekers could be sent from next year, a move that they hope will also deter more people from coming. The plan by Austria, Denmark, Germany, Greece and the Netherlands, which have spearheaded negotiations with non-EU countries, drew immediate criticism from human rights groups.

item.title: Trump arrives in Philippines to kick off Asia trip
item.description: US President Donald Trump arrived in the Philippines on Tuesday at the tail end of a Southeast Asian summit, with protests awaiting him as he prepares for the first meeting in two years of the Quad group of Indo-Pacific countries. France 24’s correspondent Tommy Walker has the details.

item.title: Candidates clash over cost of living in French presidential debate
item.description: Five of the frontrunners for the French presidential election lined up for the second of this year's debates on Monday night. In an often-rowdy debate, candidates clashed over counterproposals to raise and cut taxes and slash public spending.

item.title: She went to college to become a social worker. Now she's joined the skilled trades

item.title: Do school cellphone bans work? New study says yes – but it's complicated

item.title: France's far-right presidential candidate Le Pen to set out pension plans
item.description: France's far-right presidential candidate Marine Le Pen is to set out pension proposals on Tuesday as she seeks to convince investors she can balance one of her most popular electoral pledges ‌with promises to restore order to the public finances. Le Pen’s National Rally (RN) has pledged to allow people ⁠who started work young to retire as early as 60, although it is under pressure to detail how it would ‌do this while also curbing budget deficits.

item.title: Russia receiving ‘dozens of missiles per month’ from North Korea, says Kyiv
item.description: Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said Monday that Russia was receiving "dozens of missiles per month" from North Korea and warned that the country was taking advantage of the war to make its weapons "more effective". He called on European allies to send more weapons so that Ukraine can respond "on equal terms" to the threat.

item.title: China, Canada agree to further reduce tariffs at APEC summit in Shenzhen

The summit is also where the international agenda is enacted: Canada's Prime Minister Mark Carney has met with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping, with both leaders agreeing to reduce trade barriers between their countries. Also in this edition: Nvidia reportedly rejects a return of its former CEO Jensen Huang.
